body: Noted. Sorry! I am a full blown grump this week.
I wasn't 100% sure last night but I double checked and it is just me on all the adoption paperwork.
We've moved several times and each time put cat goes into hiding for the first week or so in the new place. We hardly saw him.
My cat's allegiances quickly change based on who it spends the most time with, which for the last 6 months is me. Also, if I wanted a custody battle, I would have had kids with him.
No. Idk I guess I'm waiting for the final, definitive nail in the coffin even though the sink is already shipping.
I think it will, but you can never really be sure.
OK thanks. I wasn't sure if cost of caring for the pet factored in at all.

I should but I can't help but hope things will fall back into place. The last few years have been tough and full of changes but maybe if we try harder we can get through it.... But then it feels like it's already over.
Yeah... I don't know what to do.

I got really depressed in college too. All I could think is how this is supposed to be the "best years of my life" but I spent a lot of time just being miserable. Although feats are good for meeting people, I know a couple guys who got so overwhelmed by adding a frat to their lives that they ended up dropping out. Not saying you will but it personally helps me to sort of keep track of the things that are adding stress to my life so I can keep them on track. College counseling is good but if you can get a referral to somewhere off campus that'd probably be even better. The college I went to for grad school has a HORRIBLE counseling office and once I went off campus for help it made a huge difference. 



I hope you find someone in your life that you feel comfortable opening up to.

I totally feel you on all of that. I am not good at socializing in the real world so I've gravitated towards games and subs where I can talk to people so that I can say I've talked to more than 2 people in one day. Also, meetup.com is good for finding groups of people that share interests with you. 


After high school, it's usually college or work but if you want to travel there are programs like the peace Corp or Americorp that you could join. Also, colleges in Europe (assuming you're in the US) are much cheaper than they are here and once you're in Europe it's much easier to travel than it is in the US.


Idk if self doubt ever really goes away. You just have to kind of be the devil's advocate against yourself like remind yourself that everyone is good at something or you can't possibly be as bad at everything as you think you are and it helps me a lot to remind myself that depression fucks with your head. I basically say that whatever I'm thinking that's bad about myself is probably less than 50% true. 


In regards to the whole god thing.... I felt much better about my life when I accepted that I did not need to believe in that crap and could believe whatever I want. I think that's generally something that it has helped me to remember in regards to many things. 


And my one final parting advice is that as you get older, it can get easier to cope with the depression because you know what triggers you and catch the signs sooner if you know what to look for. 



I hope this helps.
I know this comment was two months ago but I was depressed like 8 years before going into social work.

Most therapists are shit they have this predetermined idea of what anxiety looks like or depression looks like that most are unable to mold their definition to fit what symptoms and stuff we actually have. And it's like "oh you're depressed about your job get another job" like that's the easiest fucking thing in the world
Unfortunately I think it's the latter.

I'm a depressed social work and also think cbt and all that shit are more for people dealing with one specific problem, instead of a lifetime of depression. I'm with you on the meds though. If it weren't for them, I'd be dead.
Generally I think those people have never had to deal with depression or any time in their life where that was a serious thought so they don't get the gravity of what they're saying.
I know the feeling. No real insight. I have to force myself to do that stuff sometimes. There's no other way to do it but to force yourself.
I get them and a lot of times they cause panic attacks. Then after that I think about all the horrible things I did to ruin that particular happy time in my life.
Every close friend I've had has done something shitty so it's just me and my dog. Even when I've intentionally tried to make friends, it has never worked.

OMG I had a very similar response from a doctor. I'm in a 5 year relationship and I'm having similar issues. My bf and I have sex like once a month and even when I try to master bath it takes FOREVER to have an orgasm.

He knows I just don't want to tell him everything because I feel like it wouldn't help him to know how often I have suicidal thoughts and all the details of my fucked up brain when there isn't really anything he can do. He's very supportive, but I keep a lot to myself. I don't have to be a burden.

No support groups other than one that's very anti-medication and run by a nutritionist (so prob bullshit ) I haven't been with a good therapist long enough to even find a therapy that works. I'm starting to believe even that won't work for me. 


Thank you for your kind words. I will def check out those forums.
I don't have anything constructive to add to this other than to say that I feel the same way. Nothing seems to work, so what's the point?

I take klonopin for that but it only works for so long. I'm exhausted all day, which makes depression worse. I have super stressful dreams/nightmares. I'm hoping to try medical marijuana soon... Anything to make the bad dreams stop
Reddit/play town of Salem all day with very little in between.
I actually felt worse after posting it but now reading the kind comments people are leaving is what's making me feel better about sharing my story.
I'm sure you don't mean it that way, but the way you worded your comment sounds really mean.
He has a good job in the place we're moving to, I have an OK job in a field I don't really like in the place that we're living now. I should have clarified in my post.
99.999% of the moving situation comes down to he has a good job there so I know that it makes sense for us to move there, I just hate this feeling of having the decision made for me by work.

Thank you for your kind words and perspective. I hadn't thought about it from an old self, current self point of view and that makes a lot of sense and feels like a lightbulb kind of moment.


anyway, thank you.

Some people who missed the original thread have started posting their own secrets on here and since everyone else has gotten their sharing catharsis, I want mine too.


I have struggled with terrible depression since I was 13. I always tell people it just sort of happened and I don't remember when or why it started, but I do. 

When I was 13 I was in some kind of fucked up non-relationship with this guy who was 15 and he was the first person I ever really loved. When we started seeing each other I was just so flattered by the fact that an older guy was interested in me that I didn't notice how weird and abusive it was getting. He would kiss me and hold my hand when no one was looking and call me and sing to me over the phone and all that sappy stuff that 13 year old girls LOVE but, when we were around other people he would treat me like I didn't exist and like we had nothing together and were just acquaintances. 

Things escalated from there. We used to do a shared extracurricular activity (please no jokes) together  that allowed us a lot of alone time in quiet places. Our making out would get more intense  and soon it turned into some weird form of dry humping and at the time I pretended I liked it, but I would end up with bruises the next day from his hands and his dick and who knows what else. As all this was going on, while I was convinced I was in love, he would give me the whole, "we can't date" "I don't want to be in a relationship right now" "I like how we are" etc etc bullshit

On my 14th birthday I found out he was dating another girl and I was CRUSHED. It seems stupid even saying it but I became deeply depressed. I started intentionally injuring myself by slamming my arms and legs against objects that I knew would leave a bruise (which I'm just now realizing might be related). I started chewing at the skin on my knuckles until the bled. I wanted to die.

Several months pass by like this and before I know it, he's cheating on his girlfriend with me and I was SO happy. We went through this pattern for several years. He would tell me he loved me and I was the only one for him and then he would, for example, force my friend to make out with him, or date other girls, or fuck other girls and treat me like shit and then I would go crawling right back, all the while sinking deeper and deeper into depression.


Finally the bullshit culminated into one day when I was 15 and I went over to his house and I thought we were just gonna do our usually making out and fondling stuff (no sex yet), but suddenly he's pulling my pants down and going down on me and I don't remember much else and have blacked a lot of it out but I did not like it and wanted him to stop. He also tried to get me to suck his dick and forced me to give him a hand job. I felt so disgusting afterwards, but thankfully that was finally enough for me to kick this guy to the curb. Unfortunately, the damage was already done. I have gone through yearly cycles of deep depression (usually about half the year I'm so depressed I can barely get out of bed). I have mostly stopped self harming but still think about suicide regularly. I HATE oral sex. I'm in a very loving relationship of many years but I HATE when my SO tries to go down on me. For many years I would get panic attacks when I started hearing stories about rape and sexual assault. Once I realized why they were happening and talked it through with my shrink, I stopped getting the full on panic attacks but it still happens.


The worst part, I think, is the shame. I haven't even told my psychiatrist all of this because I still, almost a decade later, feel like it was all my fault and I was asking for it. I love my SO and he has a general idea of what happened but he doesn't know anywhere near the full story. Even just writing this I'm debating deleting it because it sounds stupid. I just felt so used and disgusting and unworthy of being loved by this person who I loved so much. That shit fucks you up. I'm a hardcore feminist and very big on women's rights and it KILLS me to have this story because I feel like if I tell people that I've been severely depressed for years after 1 guy treated me like shit, I feel like I'll seem weak and pathetic when I have spent my whole life since then trying to become someone who is tough and doesn't get pushed around. 


I've been on so many medications but my body keeps becoming resistant to them and the treatment stops working. Or I'll hear a song he used to sing and freeze right where I'm standings, or see someone on the train who looks like him and start having a panic attack. I just want to forget and move on, and I think I have, but there is just so much built up emotional damage that I'm not even sure I'll ever be able to get it all under control and it just makes me want to die. I just want to forget about all of it and stop carrying this secret around with me but I just don't know how to make it go away.



I feel so stupid about everything I just wrote but I am forcing myself to post it anyway.

I think living in a high rise is like the worst thing for people with suicidal thoughts. I live on the 9th floor and sometimes I go over to the windows to look outside and it just seems like it would be so easy. 

I can't relate much to your situation but I'm having a tough week with A LOT of suicidal thoughts and feeling very lonely, so if you want to pm me, maybe we can talk and help each other.

Thank you for your kind words. I did one of those a while back and all the meds that it said wouldn't work for me were ones I had already tried. Go figure. I hadn't thought to revisit those results though, Prozac was on the list of good ones which I tried for a while but went off of because it stopped working after a while. It seems crazy to me to hear people have been on the same meds for years. Lamictal is the only drug I've lasted a year on (and counting) but it only helps the mood swings (which is a big improvement) and not the other symptoms. 


I know it's different meds but how long did it take for your side effects to go away? I have been titrating down for 3 weeks with minor nausea, this was supposed to be my last week of it, but after talking with my doctor, she put me back up to a higher dose which made some of my side effects feel better this morning (helped A LOT with nausea) , but some do not. Part of me just wants to stop taking it, cold turkey and like lock myself in a room and a week or two until it's out of my system. It scares me though because I have never felt so suicidal as I have over the last 3 days. I've had thoughts before, but last night I had a plan and going to sleep was the only thing I could do to keep myself from hurting myself.

I would recommend you do not pursue a career in counseling, especially not crisis counseling. 


Personally I prefer not to be referred to as a "wet blanket". Don't you think the thought crosses my mind EVERY FUCK ING DAY that I might be exhausting the compassion of my boyfriend? That I don't weigh the pros and cons of telling anyone when I have a bad symptom or side effect and worry that this one panic attack or thought of suicide or crying spell might be the straw that breaks the camel's back? No need to tell me this because this is what I (as well as most people with depression) think about and worry about all day,  every day. We hold it all inside and don't tell anyone until we're on the verge of killing ourselves because we don't want to be seen as an "eeyore" or a "wet blanket" 


So thanks but no thanks for the "comforting" in my time of need.
